content: The test image shows soybean plants from above, with lower canopy leaves displaying yellow-brown angular spots and some yellowing progressing from the lower leaves upward. This pattern strongly suggests Septoria_brown_spot or Bacterial_Blight.

**Visual analysis of test image:**
- Lower canopy soybean leaves with scattered yellow-brown spots
- Angular lesion pattern visible on affected leaves
- Yellowing and early defoliation progressing from the bottom of the canopy upward
- Upper leaves appear mostly healthy/green

**Comparison with reference:**
- The Septoria reference shows a more advanced/late-season stage with widespread yellowing throughout, but the progression pattern matches
- The test image shows early-to-mid stage with angular brown-yellow spots on lower leaves — consistent with the Septoria description: "Angular, red to brown spots... Defoliation proceeds from the bottom of the plant toward the top"
- The lower-canopy-first pattern distinguishes this from Bacterial_Blight (which affects upper canopy young leaves)
- No water-soaked halos (ruling out Bacterial_Blight), no powdery coating (not Powdery_Mildew), no distinct frogeye pattern
